summary: Residency-lock refresh window causing intermittent p95 latency drift for EU traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent P95 latency increases for EU-hosted requests which correlate with residency-lock refresh windows. Traffic is pinned to eu-west but, during refresh events, a subset of requests appears to be routed via an alternate region leading to 80–200ms p95 drift.

Impact:
- NimbusAI (Dedicated customer) sees ~10% of requests in eu-west show p95 increase from 120ms to ~300ms during refresh windows.
- User-facing slowdown of synchronous features for EU users; increased error budgets on customer SLA.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool for NimbusAI
- prod (eu-west) primary
- Models: redwood-compat-v1, llama2-13b-q4f

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer sends steady 50 RPS traffic pinned to eu-west for 2 hours
2) Observe latency P95 across the interval
3) Trigger a manual residency-lock refresh (customer described as periodic backend refresh every 30m)
4) Observe spike correlated to refresh time window

Observed logs & telemetry:
- Router traces show a subset of request routes into us-east during refresh window (trace ids included below)
- No 5xx errors, but increased RTT on TLS handshake recorded for affected requests
- Control-plane logs show residency-lock heartbeats completed but with a 1–3s delay
- Dashboard links: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/latency/nimbusai-eu?from=-3h

Customer notes:
- This behavior started after an autoscaler change on their Dedicated pool (rolled 2026-02-20)
- They can reproduce reliably when they trigger a refresh from their end

Requested outcome:
- Explain root cause and provide mitigation guidance to eliminate cross-region routing during residency-lock refreshes.
- Identify any control-plane race conditions and a fix timeline.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Priya Singh (Support): Created ticket after initial customer report. Requested full pcap and example request ids; customer provided sample traces (ids: trace-8b3a, trace-8b3b).

2026-02-26 - Marco Alvarez (Oncall SRE): Initial triage indicates router re-evaluation path may run when residency metadata refresh occurs. Asked infra to check router config and route-cache invalidation logic. Assigned to Marco for investigation.

2026-02-27 - NimbusAI (Customer): Provided additional traffic profile and confirmed the refresh is initiated by their side every 30 minutes as part of cert rotation job. They report that the p95 drift only lasts ~15–30s.

2026-03-01 - Elena M. (Router Eng): Noted a race between residency-lock refresh and DNS re-resolution. If route cache TTL expires during refresh, router falls back to global resolver which prefers us-east in our config. Filed internal INT-55912 for route-cache TTL tuning.

2026-03-04 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Performed controlled repro in staging. Confirmed that when residency-lock metadata is refreshed with a 500–1500ms latency, route-cache invalidation leads to resolver fallback to us-east for ~10–40s. Added temporary mitigation toggles to avoid invalidation during refresh.

2026-03-08 - Priya Singh (Support): Shared mitigation steps with customer: disable external cert rotation during peak windows OR increase route-cache TTL to >60s and apply router patch. Customer applying patch in staging.
2026-03-10 - NimbusAI (Customer): Applied patch and observed elimination of the p95 spikes in staging. Requesting permanent fix and timeline.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Route-cache invalidation during residency-lock metadata refresh causes resolver fallback to default region -> results in cross-region routing and added RTT.
Hypothesis 2: Control-plane heartbeat delay causes temporary loss of local pool affinity, triggering smart-routing to fallback capacity in us-east.
Finding: Staging repro shows a direct correlation between metadata refresh latency (500–1500ms) and resolver fallback when route-cache TTL <= refresh latency window.
Additional finding: TLS handshake RTT contributes ~50–80ms; but main delta originates from cross-region network hop.
Dashboards consulted: per-route latency, route-cache hit ratio, control-plane heartbeats, DNS resolution times. See graph ids in related Confluence page.
Temporary mitigation verified: Increasing route-cache TTL to 120s removes resolver fallback during refresh at cost of slightly slower reaction to legitimate pool changes.

Suggested permanent fixes: 1) Delay route-cache invalidation until after residency-lock refresh completes; 2) Add optimistic sticky routing to prefer local pool if metadata was recently refreshed; 3) Improve control-plane heartbeat scheduling to avoid 1–3s delays during cert rotations.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Router patch v1.2.8 deployed to Dedicated eu-west routers on 2026-03-09 which defers route-cache invalidation during residency-lock refresh windows. Customer applied patch in staging and validated removal of p95 spikes. For production, rollout scheduled 2026-03-15 after canary checks. Follow-up: INT-55912 will track TTL tuning across clusters and a separate engineering story INF-8813 will implement sticky routing changes.
follow_up_actions: INF-8813 - Engineering story to implement optimistic sticky routing (owner: Elena M., ETA: 2026-04-07)
INT-55912 - Internal task to review route-cache TTL defaults and automated tuning (owner: Marco Alvarez, ETA: 2026-03-22)
Customer action: NimbusAI to coordinate cert rotation window with Redwood if rotation cannot be paused (contact: NimbusAI infra lead, scheduled call 2026-03-12)
